title: Cell-type-specific damage scores reveal kidney and liver disease trajectories in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no GEO/SRA links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits; only antibody and mouse-strain RRIDs (research resource identifiers) were text-mined. bioRxiv API confirms preprint 10.1101/2025.02.20.639269 (CC BY-NC-ND licence); its full text returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited), so it was not read.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: the PDS (podocyte damage score) and HDS (hepatocyte damage score) are scores computed from each cell's gene expression and applied to mostly public mouse and human single-cell, single-nucleus, spatial and proteomics datasets. A web snippet mentioned reused GEO series of liver single-nucleus data; no new deposited accession was confirmed.

a1_downloadable.note: No data accession, supplement or code link found via Europe PMC, NCBI or repository search; the paper is paywalled and the preprint full text could not be read. Not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no measured label column. The damage score would have to be recomputed per cell from expression across many reused public datasets, so the target has to be built.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are expression matrices spread across many separate GEO series that would each need downloading and harmonising; none was identified concretely.

a4_units_stated.note: The score is a unitless rank-based signature score; not checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Cell count not seen. The real unit is the sample or donor, and that number is unknown.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Several single-cell and spatial atlases; probably a few GB after subsetting to podocytes and hepatocytes, but this is unverified.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files opened, so nothing could be compared.

a8_label_provenance.note: Killer: the damage score is computed from the same gene-expression features a model would take as input, so predicting it is leakage by construction. The only measured alternative label (disease versus control condition) comes from the source studies, not from this paper.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would match the data type
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for embedding a subset of podocytes and hepatocytes
backbone.licence: Preprint is CC BY-NC-ND; licences of the reused datasets vary

integration.partner_dataset: CZ CELLxGENE Census (a public collection of single-cell datasets) for kidney and liver cells
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID / cell type ontology
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a damage axis learned in mouse models carry over to human donors? But the score itself is a fixed gene signature, so no learning task is needed.

controls.positive_control: Disease-model cells should score higher than control cells (the paper's own result).
controls.external_validation: Human single-nucleus kidney and liver cohorts (not identified concretely).

honest_claim_h3: A model trained to predict the PDS or HDS from expression would only learn to reproduce a gene-signature formula that is already computed from those same genes.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression of kidney podocytes and liver hepatocytes to predict how damaged each cell is.
plain_idea.train_on: Expression profiles of individual podocytes or hepatocytes pooled from public mouse and human datasets; count unknown.
plain_idea.predict: A per-cell damage score. In this paper the score is itself calculated from the cell's gene expression with a fixed signature, not measured separately.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Kidney and liver disease researchers could stage disease at single-cell resolution. But the paper already provides a formula for this, so a model adds nothing.

ml_idea: Considered: predicting the damage score, or the disease condition, from single-cell embeddings. Rejected because the score is a deterministic function of the inputs, and the condition labels belong to reused public datasets rather than to this paper.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data files were identified or opened.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the preprint's data availability statement: if it lists only reused GEO series and a scoring script, there is no new labelled table.

verdict_reason: A8 and A2 fail. The damage score is a gene-signature score computed from the expression features themselves, so predicting it is circular. No new deposited dataset or labelled table was found (paywalled, no PMCID, no accessions).
